classification.difficultyReason: A scaffolded geometric proof combines vector subtraction, expansion of a dot product and equal radii to establish perpendicularity.

content.prompt:
In the diagram, $O$ is the centre of a semicircle $APB$ whose diameter is $AB$.

Let $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OP}=\underset{\sim}{p}$.

spec.description: An unshaded semicircle above a diagonal diameter BA, with centre O, P near the top of the arc, and directed radii OA and OP. Ordinary source strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: O is the midpoint of diameter AB. A, P and B lie on the same circle. OA and OP are radii represented by undertilde a and p; arrows point from O to A and P. Illustrative coordinates impose no additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and vector labels are permanent question givens; no proof result or right-angle mark is supplied.

answer.worked:
Since $AB$ is the diameter, $\overrightarrow{OB}$ is a radius in the opposite direction to $\overrightarrow{OA}$. Thus

$$\overrightarrow{OB}=-\underset{\sim}{a}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Express $\overrightarrow{AP}$ and $\overrightarrow{BP}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{p}$.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\overrightarrow{BP}=|\underset{\sim}{p}|^2-|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2=0$, since $OA$ and $OP$ are radii. Hence $\angle APB=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\overrightarrow{BP}&=(\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{a})\\&=\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}\\&=\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}\\&=|\underset{\sim}{p}|^2-|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2\\&=|\underset{\sim}{p}|^2-|\underset{\sim}{p}|^2\quad\text{(equal radii)}\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$

Here $|\underset{\sim}{a}|=|\underset{\sim}{p}|$ because $\overrightarrow{OA}$ and $\overrightarrow{OP}$ represent radii of the same circle. Therefore $\overrightarrow{AP}$ and $\overrightarrow{BP}$ are perpendicular. Hence $\angle APB=90^\circ$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What circle geometry theorem have we just proven?

answer.short: An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
answer.worked: An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
